subject: Pilot extension: ops safeguard vs discount — Veridian POC
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah@veridian.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot: request for 3-week extension & packaging question

Hi Mina,

Quick note — our internal evaluation ran slightly longer than expected after we expanded the dataset for edge-case testing. We're coming up to the original 30-day pilot end date and we'd like to explore two possible paths:

1) A short extension (3 weeks) with the same ratecard but an additional 10% credit on invoiced usage at conversion.
2) An operational safeguard: keep the current end date but add 40 engineering hours of prioritized support + a short SLA bump (1% latency SLO credit) to help us finish integration.

Which of these does Redwood typically recommend for partners who need a bit more runway but want conversion-friendly terms? If you can share rough pricing delta or an example amendment, that would help our procurement conversation.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of ML, Veridian AI
sarah@veridian.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@veridian.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: request for 3-week extension & packaging question

Hi Sarah —

Really appreciate the context. Short answer: both are common; it depends whether you think the blocker is time or engineering bandwidth. A few quick notes: 

- Extension (timebox): lowest operational change, typically comes with a modest discount or conversion credit to incent close. Good if you need more runway for product validation.
- Ops safeguard (engineering hours + SLA): costs more upfront but de-risks delivery and often shortens time to value. Useful when integration complexity is the blocker.

I can put together a concise two-option amendment with concrete numbers and an attached SOW to share with procurement. Would you prefer a formal PDF for procurement or a short email summary and a call?

Sarah —

Thanks for confirming. Looping in Priyom (pricing) and David (legal/procurement) so we can move quickly. Below are two clean amendment options we've used with similar customers; I've attached a short proposal PDF and an SOW stub to accelerate procurement.

Option A — Time extension (3 weeks)
- Duration: +21 days to the current pilot end date.
- Commercial: no change to daily rate; Redwood will issue a 10% conversion credit on the first invoice if Veridian converts to a 12-month commitment within 60 days of pilot close.
- Ops: standard support window (email + 4h response for Sev 1).
- Expected lead time to sign amendment: 3–5 business days.
- Use case: more time for model parity / edge-case validation.

Option B — Operations safeguard (no extension)
- Duration: pilot end date unchanged.
- Commercial: one-time fee of $12,000 (applied as a credit toward first invoice on conversion) + delivery of 40 prioritized engineering hours from Redwood's customer success/eng team.
- SLA bump: temporary 1% latency SLO credit for the pilot window and a prioritized queue for infra changes and KV-cache tuning.
- Procurement friendliness: single amendment + SOW (attached).
- Use case: integration/troubleshooting bandwidth is the blocker; this shortens TTV and keeps commercial terms simple.

Attachments: [Attachment: veridian_pilot_proposal.pdf (PDF, 132KB)], [Attachment: redwood_sow_stub.docx (DOCX, 28KB)]

Please let me know which you prefer. If Option B looks good, David can issue a short amendment + SOW and we can route DocuSign to your procurement mailbox; if Option A, we can send a one-paragraph amendment for simpler sign-off.
